title: Approval of studded tyres with regard to their snow performance
scope_summary: The regulation approves types of new studded pneumatic tyres of Classes C1, C2 and C3 with regard to their snow performance, including snow grip marking and stud model lists. It covers tyres intended for vehicles of categories M, N and O, excluding temporary use, 'Normal' category, competition, studdable, very small/large rim and low speed-rated tyres.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to new studded pneumatic tyres of Classes C1, C2 and C3 with regard to their snow performance.
applies_to_components: tyres for use in severe snow conditions
relation_to_other_regulations: Uses definitions of UN Regulations Nos. 30 and 54, and for snow performance UN Regulation No. 117
Class C1 tyres are tyres approved according to UN Regulation No. 30; Class C2/C3 tyres are approved according to UN Regulation No. 54
Excludes temporary use tyres as declared under UN R30 and 'Normal' category of use tyres as declared under UN R30 or UN R54
Tyres shall be marked as prescribed by UN R30 or R54; approval marks may be combined with R30/R54 marks using '+' when granted by the same authority
Vehicle categories as defined in the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3)
Contracting Parties may prohibit or impose additional requirements on studded tyres

defined_terms.definition: Tyres which do not differ in manufacturer's name, tyre class, tyre structure, category of use (snow or special), tread pattern and list of stud models.
One of the groupings Class C1, C2 or C3.
Tyres approved according to UN Regulation No. 30.
Tyres approved according to UN Regulation No. 54 with load capacity index in single formation ≤ 121 and speed category symbol ≥ 'N'.
Tyres approved according to UN Regulation No. 54 with load capacity index in single formation ≥ 122, or ≤ 121 with speed category symbol ≤ 'M'.
Tyres intended to be fitted to vehicles involved in motor sport competition and not intended for non-competitive on-road use.

defined_terms.term: Tyre for use in severe snow conditions
defined_terms.definition: A tyre whose tread pattern, tread compound or structure is specifically designed for severe snow conditions and that fulfils paragraph 6.1.
A tyre designed to be equipped and always used with studs to improve traction properties on ice surfaces.
A tyre designed to be able to be equipped with studs and to be used with or without studs.
An additional device(s) inserted into or onto the tyre tread to improve traction properties on ice surfaces.
Studs that do not differ in their shape, main dimensions and mass.
The maximum height of the stud, maximum width of the stud body and maximum width of the stud bottom flange.

applicability_hints: Only tyres designed to be always used with studs fall under R164; studdable tyres (usable with or without studs) are excluded
Applies only to tyres of snow or special category of use; 'Normal' category tyres under R30/R54 are excluded
Tyres must also hold or be marked per UN R30 (C1) or UN R54 (C2/C3); class is determined by those regulations
Changing the list of stud models changes the tyre type, handled as an extension of approval
Studs themselves are not separately approved but are part of the tyre type via the list of stud models (shape, main dimensions, mass)
Excludes tyres with rim diameter code ≤ 10 or ≥ 25, speed rating below 80 km/h (F), temporary use, competition tyres, and tyres only for vehicles first registered before 1 October 1990
Snow performance testing relies on UN R117 definitions/methods
National Contracting Parties may still prohibit or restrict studded tyre use despite approval
